newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says mulls speeding up job cut plan.
newsitem.headline: KDD says mulls speeding up job cut plan.

text.p: Japanese international telecoms carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) is considering speeding up plans to reduce personnel, director Kazuyuki Tsukada told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
KDD has said it will cut personnel to 3,000 from 3,600 in its parent company by the year 2000.
The number of employees in the KDD group will be reduced to 4,800 by the year 2000 from 5,300 currently.

He said KDD plans overseas investment totalling 100 billion yen over the next five years as part of a programme to boost its overseas business to offset an expected decline in its international call services in Japan.

Tsukada said he expects the business environment to become more difficult in the 1998/99 fiscal year, following expected deregulation of international leased lines in October and entry by long-distance carriers into the international phone business.
KDD hopes to strengthen its overseas business, enter into the domestic long-distance business and aim for higher revenues for the year.
"But a profit increase might be difficult," he said.
KDD has said it expects lower profits and lower revenues in the 1997/98 fiscal year for the second consecutive year.

Tsukada said income from an undersea optic fibre cable it is building around three of Japan's main islands, the Japan Information Highway (JIH), is expected to boost overall revenues by at least 20 billion to 30 billion yen from 1999.
